text:
santosh: Heads-up — since ~03:00 UTC we've been seeing a big spike in keystore/audit egress from edge regions. NAT GW QPS up and a few us-west-2 GPU nodes failed to join with KMS_GRANT_THROTTLE. also noticing a jump in monthly egress cost projections.

maria: Ugh. Any error lines or sample logs?

santosh: Paste of kube logs: ```2026-02-24T03:12:08Z keystore-proxy ERROR decrypt failed: KMS.DecryptResourceThrottling: Rate exceeded (status=429)
stage: node-join id=i-03ab... ctx=keystore: request_id=abcd-1234
```

kevin: We pushed the default-deny firewall rule to the edge-keystore SG at 02:50 during the compliance cutover. That blocked an internal audit shipper from using the privatelink fallback, forcing it across the NAT GW.

ashley: If the shipper falls back to NAT -> KMS, it multiplies egress and KMS grant QPS. Short term options: 1) revert that SG change for the audit-shipper service only 2) enable privatelink endpoint policy for the shipper 3) ramp audit sampling down to ~20% 4) add exponential backoff + jitter in keystore decrypt path.

deploy-bot: policy-rollout: default-deny applied to security-group edge-keystore (rollout id=po-2026-02-24-02:50) :package:  

kevin: I can revert the rule but want to avoid opening a compliance hole. Could we instead add a targeted allowlist for the shipper's role/ENI?

maria: Targeted allowlist + privatelink policy is safest. Steps: create endpoint policy with principal arn:aws:iam::111222333:role/audit-shipper, attach to vpce-ks-edge, and update SG to allow only vpce-ks-edge and the shipper ENI. That will keep egress off the NAT and keep firewall tight.

ashley: Meanwhile I'll flip the audit-sampler to 25% in the shipper config and bump keystore client to 6s initial backoff with max 90s and jitter. That should reduce immediate pressure and give time for policy work.

jordan: Note: any sampling reduction needs to be recorded in the compliance tracker and we should add a Jira to revert to baseline after the cutover. I'll sign off on an exception if the runbook documents the mitigation and TTL.

kevin: OK I'm going to open a quick PR to add an SG exception for the shipper ENI (will include VPCE CIDR whitelist). PR: https://git.internal/r/infra/sg-exceptions/pulls/132. Reverting default-deny completely feels risky right now.

santosh: Timeline? we need joins unblocked in the next 30-40m or staging warm pools will get starved.

kevin: PR created, requested review from sec. Will also push a manual ephemeral allow if sec approves quicker.

maria: I created the privatelink endpoint policy draft in the console and will commit it once kevin's SG change lands. Endpoint: vpce-ks-edge-01.

ashley: Sampling update deployed to shipper at 03:28 UTC. Keystore client backoff pushed in the next minor release to staging.

kevin: Temporary SG exception applied at 03:42 UTC (rule id: ex-174824). Observability shows NAT GW QPS dropping and KMS 429s decreasing.

santosh: Confirming nodes resumed join attempts — 6/6 warm pool nodes joined by 03:55 UTC. GPU capacity trending back to normal. Thanks.

jordan: I'll open the compliance exception ticket and set a 48h TTL. Also need a postmortem entry: why default-deny rollout didn't account for privatelink principal mapping.

maria: Follow-ups: (a) finish endpoint policy PR, (b) add automated test to policy rollouts that verifies VPCE principals for audit shipper, (c) schedule a short runbook update call.

ashley: Cost note: rough estimate of the spike is ~USD 2.3k extra egress for the 12h window at current rates. We'll include in the monthly cost variance.

kevin: Reverted default-deny for edge-keystore SG entirely at 04:15 UTC after sec verbally approved while we get Endpoint policy hardened. Will reapply a tighter rule once endpoint policy + role mapping is confirmed.

santosh: Action items assigned: kevin -> finalize SG exception PR and revert policy as planned; maria -> finish endpoint policy + PR; ashley -> monitor sampling/backoff and prepare rollback; jordan -> compliance ticket + timeline.

santosh: Thanks all — keep monitoring for any further KMS GRANT throttles overnight. :thumbsup:
